startup_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me complete the first step of validating a startup idea: drafting a clear problem hypothesis and target customer profile using {{vendor}}, our AI assistant.

First, ask me for any of the following if I haven't already provided them: (1) a short description of the problem or idea I'm exploring, (2) any existing notes, customer conversations, or market observations I have, and (3) my best guess at who experiences this problem (industry, role, company size, or persona).

Then, using {{vendor}}, create a working document that includes:
1. A one-paragraph problem hypothesis stated as a falsifiable claim (e.g., "[Target customer] struggles with [specific problem] because [root cause], costing them [time/money/frustration]").
2. A target customer profile: role, context, current workaround, and why now is the right time for a solution.
3. 3-5 assumptions embedded in the hypothesis that would need to be true for the idea to work.
4. A short list of open questions to validate through customer conversations.
5. A one-sentence summary of what "invalidated" would look like (what evidence would kill this idea).

Iterate on the draft with me conversationally in {{vendor}}: ask clarifying questions if my inputs are vague, tighten the hypothesis until it's specific and testable (not generic), and revise based on any feedback I give.

Once the document is complete, export it as a file (doc or PDF) I can share with cofounders or advisors.

Report back with: a summary of the final problem hypothesis and target customer, the list of key assumptions, and confirmation that the exported document is ready along with its file name/location.

startup_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me create a landing-page smoke test to validate a startup idea before we build anything. If you don't already have these from me, ask for: (1) a one-paragraph problem hypothesis (who has the problem, what it is, why it matters), (2) my proposed solution/value proposition, (3) my target domain or subdomain if I have one, and (4) which {{vendor}} account/workspace to use (confirm you can access it with my configured credentials).

Once you have the inputs, use {{vendor}} to generate a working landing page from a natural-language description: a clear headline stating the value proposition, 2-3 supporting bullets explaining the problem/solution fit, a single primary call-to-action (e.g., 'Join the waitlist' or 'Get early access'), and an email capture form. Use {{vendor}}'s full-stack generation so the signup form actually stores submitted emails (frontend + backend from one prompt), and publish the app to a live URL in one step.

After publishing, verify the page loads correctly, the form submits successfully, and a test signup is captured/stored. Do not send real traffic or announce it yet — this step is just building and confirming the smoke test works end-to-end.

Report back with: the live URL, a summary of the page copy and CTA used, confirmation that a test signup was successfully captured, and any {{vendor}} settings I should know about (e.g., where signups are stored, how to export them). Flag anything that failed to generate or publish correctly so I can decide next steps.

startup_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me instrument signup analytics for my idea-validation landing page using {{vendor}}, so I can measure real interest before my go/no-go decision. Use your configured credentials.

First, ask me for anything missing:
- My landing page URL and where its code lives (repo, site builder, or hosted page)
- How the signup form submits (third-party form, my own backend, or an email tool)
- Whether a {{vendor}} project already exists for this site

Then do the following:
1. Install {{vendor}} on the landing page using its official web SDK or snippet. Turn on automatic capture of pageviews, clicks and form interactions where available, so I don't hand-code every event.
2. Define a small, consistent event set: landing page viewed, signup CTA clicked, signup form submitted, and signup completed. If signups are confirmed server-side, send the completed event from the backend with the official SDK so ad blockers can't drop it.
3. On successful signup, identify the user (for example by email or a stable ID) so their anonymous pre-signup activity merges into their identified profile. Attach useful properties such as traffic source/UTM parameters and plan or interest selected.
4. In {{vendor}}, create a signup funnel insight: page viewed → CTA clicked → form submitted → signup completed. Save it to a dashboard named "Idea Validation".
5. Verify end to end. Submit a test signup, confirm each event arrives in order with the right properties, confirm the anonymous and identified activity merged, and confirm the funnel shows the test conversion. Then mark or exclude the test user so it doesn't skew results.

Done looks like this: tracking is live on the production page, all four events fire, identity merge works, and the funnel insight is saved.

Report back with:
- The events and properties you created
- The files or settings you changed
- A link to the funnel insight
- Your test results
- Any gaps, such as ad-blocker loss or missing UTM capture, with your recommended fixes

startup_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare and track customer interviews for validating my startup idea. The actual live conversations with prospects remain a human step — you cannot conduct them.

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing: my problem hypothesis/one-line pitch, target customer profile, my domain or landing page URL (if live), and a list or count of prospects I've lined up (names/emails/company if available).

Then prepare the following:
1. A concise interview script: 5-8 open-ended, non-leading questions probing the problem's severity, current workarounds, willingness to pay, and buying process — tailored to my hypothesis.
2. A short outreach email/DM template to schedule interviews (subject line + body), referencing my landing page or pitch if provided.
3. A tracking sheet (as a table or CSV-ready text) with columns: prospect name, contact info, status (not contacted / scheduled / completed / no-show), scheduled date/time, and a notes field for key insights.
4. A post-interview synthesis template with sections for pain points, quotes, objections, and a validation signal (strong/weak/no signal).

Once these are drafted, present them to me for review and then stop for human sign-off before I send any outreach or conduct interviews myself — this conversational step remains a human step.

After I've actually held the interviews, I will come back and share raw notes or summaries with you. At that point, help me populate the tracking sheet and synthesis template, look for patterns/themes across interviews, and flag whether the aggregate evidence supports a go or no-go call on the idea.

Report back with: the drafted script, email template, tracking sheet, and synthesis template, plus a clear note that live interviews and outreach sending are pending my action and require me to confirm completion before you proceed to synthesis.

startup_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me validate my startup idea by analyzing signup data and interview notes together. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) my landing-page domain, (2) which product-analytics tool I'm using as {{vendor}} (e.g., I'll tell you the specific one), (3) confirmation that you have access via my configured credentials, and (4) the location or content of my prospect interview notes (doc link or pasted text).

Once you have these, use {{vendor}}'s export or query API (via documented API/MCP access) to pull raw signup event data and any available user profile or aggregate visitor stats. Analyze this data to answer: How many visitors converted to signups? Where in the activation funnel do users drop off most? Are there patterns by traffic source, device, or timing? Do not invent metrics not present in the data.

Then read through the interview notes and extract: recurring pain points, objections, language prospects use to describe the problem, and any stated willingness to pay. Correlate these qualitative themes with the quantitative signup/drop-off patterns — for example, does a stated objection map to a specific funnel drop-off point?

Produce a concise report (under one page) with: (1) key funnel/conversion numbers, (2) top 2-3 drop-off points, (3) top 2-3 recurring interview themes, (4) explicit connections between the data and the interviews, and (5) a plain-language recommendation on whether the evidence supports proceeding, pivoting, or killing the idea.

Report back with this summary and flag any data gaps (e.g., insufficient signup volume, missing tracking) that limit confidence in the conclusions.

startup_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a go/no-go decision packet for my startup idea validation process. I have already run a landing-page smoke test with signup instrumentation and talked to prospective customers. Please help me compile and organize the evidence into a clear decision-ready summary, but do NOT make or record the actual go/no-go decision — that is my call to make.

If you don't already have these from me, ask for: (1) my landing page URL and the analytics/signup tool I used (e.g., Google Analytics, Mixpanel, ConvertKit, Typeform) so you can pull traffic, conversion, and signup numbers via my configured credentials; (2) notes or transcripts from customer conversations; (3) my original problem hypothesis statement; (4) any target thresholds I set beforehand (e.g., minimum conversion rate, number of signups, number of validating customer quotes).

Using this, produce a one-page decision memo with: a summary of the problem hypothesis, key quantitative results (traffic, conversion rate, signup count) compared against my stated thresholds, a synthesis of qualitative themes from customer conversations (pain intensity, willingness to pay, objections), and a clear side-by-side of evidence supporting 'go' versus evidence supporting 'no-go.' Include a checklist of open questions or risks I should weigh before deciding.

Do not recommend a final decision, do not draft any commitment language (e.g., hiring plans, funding asks, building tickets) as if approved, and do not take any action that commits resources. Once the memo and checklist are ready, stop for human sign-off and report back with the compiled memo, the data sources used, and any gaps in evidence you found while assembling it.

startup_001:n1b.prompt:
You are helping me capture our startup's hypothesis doc in {{vendor}}, our chosen project-management workspace, as part of validating a new idea before we build anything. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) the one-sentence problem hypothesis, (2) target customer segment, (3) the riskiest assumption we're testing, (4) the success/failure criteria for the go/no-go call, and (5) which {{vendor}} workspace or parent page the doc should live under.

Once I provide these, draft a structured hypothesis doc with these sections: Problem Hypothesis, Target Customer, Key Assumptions (ranked by risk), Smoke Test Plan (landing page + signup instrumentation approach), Success Metrics, and Go/No-Go Criteria. Write it in clear, concise language suitable for a shared team doc.

Using my configured credentials, create this as a new page in {{vendor}} by calling the page-creation API (the operation that creates a new page, e.g. POST /v1/pages if that's the exact API in use) with the parent set to the workspace/page I specified, and populate the page body with the sections above as structured content (headings, bullet lists).

Done looks like: a single new {{vendor}} page exists containing all six sections filled in with my inputs, properly formatted, and located under the correct parent page/workspace.

Report back with: the page title, its direct {{vendor}} URL, and a short summary confirming each section was populated. If any input was missing or ambiguous, note what you assumed so I can correct it before we proceed to the smoke test step.
